title: This Salmon Swims 2,000 Miles Upstream Without Eating

scenes.text: This fish swims two thousand miles upstream. And it never eats.
It's the king salmon, and its trip starts in the Bering Sea.
It fights the current for about sixty days.
It stops feeding the moment it enters fresh water, and burns its own body fat to keep going.
At the end, it spawns in the stream where it was born.
Two thousand miles on an empty stomach.

description:
A king salmon can swim more than 2,000 miles up the Yukon River in about 60 days, and it does not eat on the way.
It lives off stored body fat until it reaches the stream where it was born.
Could you go a day without food?
first_comment: Bonus: the biggest king salmon on record weighed 126 pounds. Would you swim 2,000 miles for your hometown?
